chunks: (3) Three narrators - And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id told us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan at-Taymali told me, saying: Al-Hasan and Muhammad, the sons of Ali ibn Yousuf, narrated to us, from their father, from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Salih ibn Abul Aswad, from Abu al-Jarood, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far saying:

None of us, the Ahl al-Bayt, who repels an oppression or invites to truth, unless calamity strikes him down until a group rises that fought in Badr, whose killed are not buried and whose wounded are not cured. I said: 'Whom did Abu Ja'far mean by that?' He said: 'The angels.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيْتِ: Ahl al-Bayt (the People of the House)

ai.seo_question: Who are the angels that fought in Badr according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) explains that the Ahl al-Bayt are protected from calamity only after a specific group rises, identified here as the angels who fought at Badr. This highlights the Shia eschatological concept of divine intervention and the unique status of the Imams, whose trials are distinct from the general faithful until the final victory. The reference to Badr underscores the continuity of divine support from the Prophet's era to the emergence of the Mahdi.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (3) Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Sa’eed narrated from Ali bin al-Hasan at-Taymali from al-Hasan and Muhammad the sons of Ali bin Yousuf from their father from Ahmad bin Ali al-Halabi from Salih bin Abul Aswad that Abul Jarood had said: I heard Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) saying:

“None of us, Ahlul Bayt, resisting an oppression or inviting for a truth, unless death is his end until a group, that has fought in the battle of Badr and whose killed ones are not buried and whose wounded ones are not cured, rises.” I said: “Whom do you mean?” He said: “The angels.”
